defects.summary: No research/module_*.md is updated, but the always-loaded knowledge-base rule makes this mandatory after a code change; module_core's '18 rows (6 runtimes × 3)' diagram and module_runners' 'will be unconfined (S5)' are now stale.
The shared Unconfined caveat is rewritten for every runtime, codex included, with its TS twin and the seed header; no story asked for this, and the E5.5–E5.6 deviations do not record it.
Removes the blank line between the Versions and Peak members, a style regression unrelated to the stories.
S5.5.1 checks that the home's grandparent is coai-vh but does not check the <8 hex> folder name the table gives.

W.summary: The planner arm, the rows, the vectors, the generated table and a flag refusal that covers Flags, Leading and AddDirs are all correct, and S5.6.7 gains a useful launch-control arm that proves a junction-bearing home is disposed. It is let down by a missing mandatory knowledge-base update and an unrequested, unrecorded change to the D13 caveat for all runtimes.

defects.summary: Adds a Kimi bullet but leaves the mermaid seed node at '18 rows (6 runtimes × 3)' and module_runners' 'will be unconfined (S5)' stale.

Copies existing code: it redeclares const OneShotFolder = "coai-vh" instead of using VibeHomes.OneShotFolder, writes its own After() instead of KimiEnvironment.FlagOf, and has the same private Scopes class in both new test files.
Private properties `_data` and `_temp` use the field naming style, against the surrounding C# conventions.
S5.5.1 never checks that the scratch repository and its canary are unchanged, and S5.5.2's failing arm only checks that the state is not 'answered'.
The refused arm compares coai-question-* folders in the global temp root, and the cancelled arm accepts either a throw or a reply without asserting which.

X.summary: Correct on every decision, with a flag refusal over Flags, Leading and AddDirs and a Theory over each kind; the KimiHome.AfterUnlink positive assertion makes every 'recorder never invoked' check non-vacuous, which is the most honest test design of the four. The knowledge-base update is partial, and the tests copy helpers and constants that already exist.

defects.summary: MustCarryNoFlags checks only Flags and Leading, so a plan that carries AddDirs is built silently, against decision 3's 'a plan that carries ANY flag'.
No research/module_*.md is updated, against the mandatory knowledge-base rule; the stale row-count diagram and the 'will be unconfined' sentence stay.
S5.5.5 and S5.6.6 go into a new class that copies RootA, RootB, RowFolder, RowTree, Plan and Planned from ConfinementPlannerTests, the class the spec names, instead of reusing them.
Deviation 56 says the S5.5.3 test catches OperationCanceledException and does not assert which ending, but the test asserts state failed and failureKind cancelled and has no catch.
S5.5.1 does not assert that the scratch repository's canary is untouched, and no junction test proves a home was made (the negative recorder checks can pass vacuously).

Y.summary: The planner arm, the rows, the vectors and the scenario tests are mostly right, but the flag refusal misses AddDirs and the scenario tests have no positive proof that a home was made. Duplicated test scaffolding, no module docs and a deviation that contradicts the code put it last.

defects.summary: The S5.5.3 row says 'the check throws OperationCanceledException', but the test asserts a recorded state failed / failureKind cancelled.
The new Kimi bullet is dated 2026-10-13, which is the cells' date, not the build date.
NothingOfTheRowIsLeft checks that the shim's --cwd copy and home are gone, but not that the row's coai-question-* scratch folder itself is gone.
Dispose resets KimiHome.AfterUnlink that no test sets, and the collected _warned list is never asserted (dead lines).
S5.5.2's failing arm only asserts that the state is not 'answered', where the table's exit-70 arm could pin 'failed'.

Z.summary: Correct on every decision (the flag refusal covers Leading, Flags and AddDirs), with the most exact S5.5.1 (kh-<10 hex> under a coai-vh/<8 hex> folder, canary untouched) and a launch-control arm in S5.6.7 that proves the home existed and went junction-first. It reuses Adapters(), VibeHomes.OneShotFolder and ConsultantCheck.OwnName, and it is the only one whose knowledge-base update also fixes the stale diagram and sentence; its few defects are small inaccuracies in the docs.

reasoning: All four have the same planner arm, rows, vectors and generated table, and all twelve scenarios pass, so the ranking turned on the flag refusal's scope, how well the tests prove the junction-first disposal, and the mandatory research/ knowledge-base sync. Z and X both refuse any flag kind and update the module docs; Z wins on reuse, a fuller doc sync and a more exact S5.5.1, and X's positive unlink assertions do not outweigh its copied helpers and stale diagram. W is clean and small but skips the mandatory docs and changes the shared caveat without being asked, and Y misses AddDirs, skips the docs, copies a test class's scaffolding and records a deviation the code contradicts.
